_readme: The words for the random events, plus a few of Sam's everyday actions. When each event can happen and what its choices do stay in js/events/random.js.
Any text can be a single string or a list (one is picked at random). Placeholders are filled in by the game: {name} = the lady involved, plus the extras listed in each event's _vars.
Keep the choice keys as they are (they're how the code finds them); change the label and result wording freely.
image (optional): {comp, setting, sam} a picture for that event instead of a generic scene.

haunt.title: {house}: Things That Go Bump
text: Every candle in the east wing lights itself at midnight. Three guests faint. Four ask if they can book that room again.
A portrait in the hallway has started winking at guests. Business is up.
Something rearranged all the furniture in the lounge overnight. Into a much better layout, honestly.

lean.label: Lean into it
lean.res: Word spreads. Thrill-seekers line up. +house popularity.

exorcist.label: Call an exorcist (60g)
exorcist.resGhost: The exorcist leaves in tears. {ghost} is offended you asked.

image.comp: translucent ghostly woman drifting through a wall with a mischievous grin, guests fleeing in the background
image.setting: lantern-lit lounge at night, cold blue glow

dayoff.title: A Small Request
dayoff.text: {name} catches you in the hallway. "Could I take a few days off? I'm running on fumes."

no.label: Not this week
no.resSoft: {name} says she understands. She looks very tired.
no.res: {name} nods stiffly and goes back to work.

image.comp: slumped at a kitchen table with her head on her arms, tired eyes, untouched cup of tea
image.setting: quiet staff kitchen in the early morning

noble.title: A Noble Invitation
noble.text: A messenger in house livery requests {name}'s company for a private dinner at a nobleman's estate. The offered fee: {gold}.

ask.label: Ask her if she wants to go
ask.res: {name} agrees and returns the next morning with the fee and a smug smile. +{gold}, +renown.
ask.pass: {name} politely passes. You send regrets. She appreciates being asked.

image.comp: holding a wax-sealed parchment invitation, curious half-smile
image.setting: velvet lounge, warm candlelight

guild.title: Guild Celebration
guild.text: Hanna sends word: a party just cleared a dungeon floor and wants company for their victory feast. They asked for {name} by name. Fee: {gold}.

send.label: Send {name}
send.res: It goes great. {name} comes back with the fee and three new admirers. +{gold}.

pass.label: Pass this time
pass.res: Hanna sends back a sad-face doodle.

image.comp: standing at a busy guild counter accepting a sealed contract, adventurers around her
image.setting: bustling adventurers' guild hall, notice boards

poach.title: An Offer from the Thorn
poach.text: {name} admits Isolde Thorne offered her a position at the Velvet Thorn, with better pay. She hasn't decided.

raise.label: Offer a raise (+30%)
raise.res: {name} stays. "Okay. You actually value me. Noted."

talk.label: Talk it through
talk.stay: You talk for an hour. {name} decides she'd rather stay.

image.comp: holding a fancy embossed letter, conflicted expression, glancing at a rival's calling card
image.setting: quiet hallway, afternoon light

lucky.title: Lucky Break
text: A regular leaves a coin purse "as a tip." It holds {gold}.
You find {gold} hidden behind a loose brick in the cellar. The old owner had secrets.
A merchant pays {gold} for the ugliest painting in the house. Nobody asks why.

inspector.title: The Inspector
inspector.text: A city inspector with a clipboard announces you owe "licensing fees." He says {gold}, but he sounds like he's improvising.

argue.label: Argue the paperwork
argue.win: You cite three ordinances that don't exist with total confidence. The inspector leaves, confused. No fee.
argue.lose: It does not go well. {fine} and a lecture.

friends.title: Friends
friends.text: {name} and {other} have started taking their breaks together. Things feel a bit warmer.

image.comp: laughing with another woman over cards at a table, relaxed and happy
image.setting: staff common room in the evening, warm lamplight

quiet.title: A Quiet Moment
quiet.text: {name} finds you on the back steps after closing and sits next to you. "You know, you're not what I expected. In a good way."

stay.label: Stay and talk
stay.res: You sit together and watch the two moons rise.

image.comp: sitting on the back steps next to him sharing a pot of tea, talking quietly, shoulders touching
image.setting: back steps of an inn at dusk, lanterns coming on, town rooftops

raise.title: Raise Request
raise.text: {name} plants herself in front of your desk. "I'm worth more than {wage} a week, and we both know it. {newWage}."

refuse.label: Refuse
refuse.resProud: {name} stares at you for a long, cold moment. She won't forget this.

image.comp: standing in front of a desk with arms folded, determined expression, a list of her accomplishments in hand
image.setting: small office, lamplight

incident.title: Trouble at {house}
incident.text: A drunk adventurer starts shoving furniture and shouting about a refund for a service he never actually paid for.

guard.label: Let {guard} handle it
guard.res: {guard} throws him out in about four seconds. The regulars applaud.

sam.label: Step in yourself
sam.win: You talk him down. Mostly by being so polite it's confusing. +house popularity.
sam.lose: You take a punch, then the drunk falls asleep on his own. You get a black eye and a lot of sympathy.

pay.label: Pay for the damage
pay.res: Broken chairs and a cracked mirror: {gold}.

chat._note: What Sam and a lady talk about when he chats with her. home is used for ladies from Sam's old world. ng is mixed in from New Game+ (cycle 2+).
topics: about the strangest client of the week
about your old world. She refuses to believe in trains
about what she wants to do with her life
about whether "isekai" is a real word (she insists it is not)
home: about home, and what you both miss most
ng: about the returners everyone at the guild is suddenly talking about
about whether she'd want to remember, if she came back
about the Lantern Stone, and why it keeps lighting
about a dream she keeps having where she already knows you

outfit_market.title: A Find at the Market
text: {name} comes back from the market with a bundle under her arm. "I found {outfit}. It was practically calling my name, and I got it for almost nothing."
{name} holds up {outfit}, still folded from the stall. "Look what I found. The seller had no idea what it was worth."

keep.label: "It suits you."
res: She hugs the bundle to her chest. {outfit} is hers.

share.label: "Put it in the house wardrobe."
res: {name} shrugs happily. "Then everyone can borrow it." {outfit} joins the house wardrobe.

image.comp: standing in front of a full-length mirror modeling her new outfit with a delighted smile
image.setting: lantern-lit market stall clearing, colorful fabric awnings

outfit_regular.title: A Present from a Regular
text: A parcel arrives at the front desk, addressed to {name}. Inside is {outfit} and a note: "For a lady with good taste. - an admirer."
One of {name}'s regulars has left a gift for her at the door: {outfit}, wrapped in tissue paper.

keep.label: "Keep it, it's yours."
res: {name} tries it on in front of the mirror, delighted. {outfit} is hers.

share.label: "Let the house share it."
res: {name} thinks about it, then nods. {outfit} goes into the house wardrobe, and the regular's note goes on the wall.

image.comp: turning beside a gilded mirror in her new outfit, unwrapping tissue ribbon, pleased smile
image.setting: bright dressing parlor with warm lamps

outfit_friend._vars: {name} = the lady, {other} = her friend, {outfit} = the outfit
outfit_friend.title: Borrowed Finery
text: {other} presses {outfit} into {name}'s hands. "It never fit me right. You take it."
"Try this on," says {other}, handing {name} {outfit}. "I've had it for ages. It was made for someone with your look."

share.label: "Hang it in the house wardrobe."
res: {other} laughs. "Fine, fine. Anyone can wear it, then." {outfit} joins the house wardrobe.

image.comp: posing playfully in her new outfit for a friend, smiling brightly
image.setting: staff bedroom with wooden wardrobe and warm lamplight

outfit_made.title: Handmade
text: {name} spent her evenings with a needle and a bolt of cloth. She holds up the result: {outfit}. "I made it myself. What do you think?"
{name} lays something across the kitchen table, stitched by candlelight: {outfit}. "It took a while, but I'm proud of it."

keep.label: "It's wonderful. Wear it."
res: {name} glows. {outfit} is hers, and she made it.

share.label: "Let the whole house enjoy it."
res: {name} blushes and nods. {outfit} goes into the house wardrobe.

image.comp: standing beside a wooden kitchen table in her freshly tailored outfit, glowing with quiet pride
image.setting: warm kitchen and sewing table, soft candlelight

gift._note: When Sam gives a lady a gift. The gift itself comes from people.json gifts.
normal: She smiles and tucks it away carefully.

returners._note: New Game+ only (cycle 2+). Word spreads that people come back. {name} = a lady, {cycle} = the cycle number, {gold}.

rumor.title: A Word for It
text: Hanna leans over the guild counter, far too pleased with herself. "So there's a word going round. Returners. People who swear they've lived this year before. A smith on Copper Row who knew which blade would crack. A barmaid who greeted a stranger by name." She taps her quill against her teeth. "You wouldn't know anything about that, would you, Mr. Takahashi?"

A drunk at the bar is holding court: a man who woke up knowing the river would flood, and sold boats a week early. "Returners," someone says, and three people at the next table go very quiet and very interested in their drinks.

listen.label: Ask what else people are saying
listen.res: More than you'd think. A healer in the Underdistrict, two sisters who run a stall by the gate, a knight who keeps calling his squire by the wrong name. Nobody agrees on why. Everyone agrees it's getting more common. (+renown)

deflect.label: Laugh it off
deflect.res: "Sounds exhausting," you say. The look you get back says you aren't fooling anyone, but the conversation moves on.

image.comp: leaning over a guild counter whispering gossip, quill in hand, conspiratorial grin
image.setting: busy adventurers' guild hall, notice boards

deja.title: Déjà Vu
text: {name} stops halfway through setting a table, a plate in each hand. "I've done this before," she says slowly. "Not this table. This moment. You were standing right there, and you said..." She frowns. "I don't remember what you said. Only that I liked it."

{name} wakes you before dawn, sitting on the end of your bed. "I had the strangest dream. We'd already met. I already knew how you take your tea." She holds up the cup she brought you. It's exactly right.

truth.label: Tell her the truth
truth.res: It takes a while, and a second pot of tea. {name} doesn't laugh. "That explains a lot," she says finally, and leans her head on your shoulder. "Then I picked you twice. Good taste."

smile.label: Say it's a good dream
smile.res: "It is," {name} agrees, and doesn't push. But she keeps glancing at you for the rest of the day, like she's checking you against a memory.

image.comp: pausing mid-motion with a soft, puzzled, nostalgic smile, holding a teacup
image.setting: quiet kitchen at dawn, pale window light

familiar.title: A Familiar Face
text: A grey-bearded merchant stops you at the door, squinting. "We've met. I'd swear to it. You ran a place like this, and I left too large a tip because you remembered my wife's name." He presses a coin purse into your hand. "Call it making up for a life I can't quite recall." (+{gold})

A woman in travelling clothes orders a drink, takes one look at you, and laughs. "It's you. The hoodie. You don't remember me, do you? Never mind. You were kind to me once, somewhere else." She overpays and won't take the change. (+{gold})

lamp.title: The Lantern Stone
lamp.text: Anael finds you at the crossroads after close. The old Lantern Stone is burning, steadier than before. "It has been lit {cycle} times now," she says. "The Order's records only allow for once. I have been instructed to file a correction." She looks at the flame, then at you. "I have not decided what the correction should say."

stay.label: Stay with her a while
stay.res: You watch the flame together until the bells ring midnight. When Anael finally writes her report, it is three pages long and none of it is about the lamp.

ask.label: Ask what the Order thinks it means
ask.res: "That souls who arrive unsent sometimes refuse to leave," Anael says. "And that the world bends a little to keep them." A pause. "The Order considers this a problem. I find I don't."

image.comp: standing beside a glowing stone lantern at night, soft halo light, thoughtful expression, looking at him
image.setting: quiet crossroads at midnight, ancient stone lantern burning

circle.title: The Returners' Circle
circle.text: A folded card arrives with no seal, only a hand-drawn lantern and an address above a teahouse. Inside: a dozen people who all, in one way or another, should not remember what they remember. A former schoolteacher. A sellsword who apologises to everyone. A woman who still checks her pockets for a phone. Someone hands you tea. "Welcome back," they say, and it's clear they've said it many times before.

join.label: Become a regular
join.res: The Circle meets on the last night of each month. People talk, and some of them are looking for work. (+renown. Someone else who doesn't belong to this world is already waiting among your candidates.)

visit.label: Just stay for the tea
visit.res: It's good tea. You leave with a full stomach and a strange, light feeling, like being remembered by strangers.

townEvents._note: Town events (balance.json → townEvents has the numbers, label and desc). One page when an event starts; the label/desc and its length are added under the text. {weeks} = how long it runs. Lists pick one at random.

festival.title: The Lantern Festival
text:
Paper lanterns go up along every street in Hollowmere overnight, strung roof to roof until the whole city glows orange after dark. Stalls crowd the squares, the taverns stop closing, and the roads in are thick with visitors who came for the lights and stay for the nights.

A crier on the corner shouts the festival schedule twice an hour. Busiest weeks of the year, everyone tells you. Also the rowdiest.

You wake to drums. The Lantern Festival has started a day early, and by noon there are so many strangers in the streets that you can barely cross to the market. Every one of them has coin and nowhere to spend the night.

It's good for business. It's also a lot of drunk men far from home.

choices.label: Light extra lanterns and welcome the crowd
choices.res: You hang extra bulbs along every rail and throw the doors open wide to the festival surge.

choices.label: Hire extra door watch (-120g, lower pushy risk)
choices.broke: Your purse won't stretch for extra bouncers, so you work with the crowd as it comes.

overrides.desc: Clients flock to Hollowmere (+25% demand, +20% propositions) while hired bouncers keep pushy risk down (-10%).

choices.res: Two off-duty pit guards lean silently beside your door—plenty of festival coin, far fewer headaches.

choices.label: Run high-end festival bottles (-80g, lift class & fees)
choices.broke: Not enough gold for vintage cases, so you stick to house pours.

overrides.desc: Festival demand rises (+20%), wealthy guests spend more (+15%), pushy incidents rise 15%.

choices.res: You stock the bar with festival vintages and turn a noisy street fair into heavy spending.

austerity.title: A Credit Audit
text:
A clerk from the Vane Credit House arrives with a ledger under one arm and a list of every business in the district. The Credit House is auditing its borrowers, and for the next few weeks every supplier in town wants payment up front and a little extra for the trouble.

The merchants and nobles who still come through your door, though, are in a generous mood. Nothing makes a rich man spend like watching his rivals count coppers.

choices.label: Tighten the books cleanly
choices.res: You mark every ledger twice and lean on high-spending regulars to carry the audit weeks.

choices.label: Prepay suppliers in bulk (-180g, soften upkeep)
choices.broke: You don't have the reserve coin to lock rates early, so upkeep stings as normal.

overrides.desc: Bulk prepay keeps upkeep near normal (+5%) while merchants and nobles pay 20% more.

choices.res: Two early wagons settle the cellar and laundry contracts cleanly before rates spike across town.

choices.label: Offer quiet rebates to repeat nobles (+house renown)

overrides.desc: Upkeep +20%, +10% demand and +15% rich patron fees while noble regulars pack the suites.

choices.res: Your private regulars spread word through every manor dining room that your parlor runs undisturbed.

warm_winds.title: Warm Winds
text:
A hot wind comes up from the south and doesn't leave. The nights stay sticky, nobody sleeps well, and the ladies drift around the house in as little as they can get away with. Tempers run short. Everything else runs high.

You catch yourself staring more than once. So do they.

choices.label: Throw the shutters open
choices.res: You prop every casement wide and keep cold mint water in the pitcher.

choices.label: Set out iced linens and citrus tea (-90g, ease mood)
choices.broke: No spare coin for ice blocks this week—everyone fans themselves through the heat.

overrides.desc: Staff lust builds 35% faster and lewdness grows 25% quicker, without mood dragging.

choices.res: Ice pitchers and thin linen keep everyone comfortable while the heat settles straight into everyone's pulse.

iron_watch.title: City Watch Crackdown
text:
The City Watch doubles its patrols after a brawl in the Underdistrict ends in a fire. Armored pairs walk past your door every hour, and the clients who like to push their luck have suddenly found their manners.

The flip side: every lady looking for work knows the Watch is checking papers, and the ones willing to sign anywhere want more for the risk.

choices.label: Keep heads down while patrols pass
choices.res: Nobody tests your doors with armored pairs marching past every hour.

choices.label: Invite the watch sergeant for house tea (-60g, softer hiring)
choices.broke: No coin for an impression gift, so your ladies keep papers handy the normal way.

overrides.desc: Pushy risk drops 45%, while signing fees barely budge (+5%).

choices.res: A polite cup of tea and clean paperwork keep patrols waving fondly at your entrance instead of staring at new arrivals.

scholars.title: Academy Exams
text:
Exam season at the city's academies. The city fills with tutors, crib sheets and nervous students, and every bookshop runs late. For a few weeks, anyone who wants to learn something can find someone to teach it, cheap.

The downside is the clientele: the students are broke and too busy to visit, and the town is talking about grades instead of your houses.

choices.label: Clear an afternoon table for study notes
choices.res: Quills scratch through the afternoon lull while everyone sharpens their craft.

choices.label: Hire a visiting rhetoric tutor (-100g, boost lessons)
choices.broke: You pass on the tutor's fee and let everyone read what they have.

overrides.desc: Training and classes jump +55%; town renown rises only slightly slower (-10%).

choices.res: An academy fellow happily trades crisp coaching for gold—turning a slow street into the sharpest week of the month.

crimson_nights.title: Crimson Nights
text:
The moon rises red three nights running. The old women in the market say it's a lucky omen for lovers; the priests say it's just dust from the south. Either way, you feel wide awake, and the ladies are softer with you than usual, lingering when they pass you in the hall.

You don't question it.

choices.label: Stay up late with them
choices.res: You walk every floor after midnight and find smiles lingering at every landing.

choices.label: Host a quiet wine night in the lounge (+mood)

overrides.desc: Sam gets +20 max energy and everyone builds trust 35% faster under the red moon.

choices.res: One shared decanter under the red moonlight melts half the week's guarded edges right away.

merchant_fleet.title: Merchant Fleet in Port
text: Three tall spice galleons drop anchor before dawn, and before noon every factor, shipmaster, and well-heeled passenger is walking up the hill toward the Lantern Quarter with fresh salt on his boots and heavy silver purses in his coat.

choices.label: Welcome the captains and factors as they land
choices.res: Your hosts clear the best parlor tables before the fleet's bell even finishes ringing.

choices.label: Reserve suites for shipmasters (-120g, boost prestige & rich fees)
choices.broke: No reserve gold to deck out suites early; the fleet still crowds your bar.

overrides.desc: Fleet traffic lifts demand +15%, while merchant and noble shipmasters spend 35% more.

choices.res: Silver trays and private carriage escort pull the richest captains straight through your front doors.

choices.label: Run dockside leaflets for the crew (more demand)

overrides.desc: Sailors and merchants pack the door (+30% demand, +15% rich fees, +10% pushy risk).

choices.res: Half the docks know your corner by dusk, keeping every room hopping past midnight.

harvest_fair.title: The Harvest Fair
text: Wagons of pressed cider, autumn pears, and roasted chestnuts ring the market plaza for the Harvest Fair. Farmers come in flush from the crop sales, musicians camp beside every fountain, and the whole district stays warm and flush until midnight.

choices.label: Put spiced cider and warm pies out for the house
choices.res: The whole parlor smells of cloves and roasted orchard fruit for weeks.

choices.label: Send your ladies out early for fair samples (+house renown)

overrides.desc: Fair traffic lifts demand +25% and mood +3 a week (+10% upkeep for fair stock).

choices.res: Smiles and fair tokens bring back a cheerful flood of guests with coin still jingling in their pockets.

choices.label: Keep kitchens modest to save coin

overrides.desc: Fair visitors lift demand +15% and mood +1 without inflating house upkeep.

choices.res: You skip the expensive spice barrels and let the fair crowds do the work.

rainy_spell.title: Monsoon Week
text: Low grey clouds park directly over Hollowmere and open into a warm, drumming downpour that turns every cobble black and slick. Casual strollers vanish indoors—leaving quiet afternoons perfect for drills, lessons, and close quarters under a dry roof.

choices.label: Use the quiet afternoons for study and practice
choices.res: Rain beats against the shutters while everyone drills patiently beside the hearth.

choices.label: Light extra braziers to keep the lounge inviting (-80g, soften traffic drop)
choices.broke: Not enough coin for extra charcoal hampers; you let the rain keep the street quiet.

overrides.desc: Warm lounges limit the rain dip (-5% demand) while training +20% and lust +20%.

choices.res: Warm cedar smoke pouring out under the awning tempts cold pedestrians straight inside out of the wet.

masquerade.title: Quarter Masquerade
text: Every parlor on Lantern Row hangs silk banners for the autumn masquerade—half the patrons arrive in feathered masks, half the staff wears domino lace, and bold offers fly twice as fast once names stop mattering behind velvet.

choices.label: Hand out silk dominoes at the door
choices.res: Anonymity loosens every tongue and makes even quiet guests surprisingly daring.

choices.label: Set clear house rules at the velvet ropes (+mood, steady security)

overrides.desc: Propositions rise 20% and lewdness +15%, while clear boundaries keep pushy trouble down (-5%).

choices.res: Everyone keeps the masks playful instead of grabbing hands, keeping propositions bold without chaos.

choices.label: Join the revelry without boundaries (+200g upfront bar tips)

overrides.desc: Wild masquerade nights (+35% propositions, +25% lewdness growth, +25% pushy risk).

choices.res: Corks pop before dark and masks fly off upstairs while gold pours over the bar.

alley_rumor.title: Alleyway Gossip at {house}
text: Someone started a petty street rumor claiming {house} watered down its parlor wine and turned away regulars last Tuesday. It's nonsense, yet half the market taverns are repeating it before dusk.

choices.label: Let the work speak for itself and ignore it
choices.res: You shrug at the barkeep's gossip and keep your rooms spotless until the talk dies down.

choices.label: Pour free tastings on the corner to squash it (-110g, clear the rumor early)
choices.broke: You don't have the coin for free cellar pours right now—everyone has to ride out the talk.
choices.res: Two open casks and honest laughter on the corner shut the rumor down flat before sunset.

choices.label: Turn the talk into intrigue (+mood, smaller demand hit)

overrides.desc: Curiosity limits gossip at {house} (-5% demand only, reputation unaffected).

choices.res: You send your sharpest promoter out smiling; curious newcomers wander past {house} just to see for themselves.

noble_patronage.title: A Noble's Favor at {house}
text: A notoriously picky count leaves {house} with a wide smile and immediately brags about the service at three private club dinners. Overnight, titled gentlemen and guild factors are asking specifically which carriages stop at {house}.

choices.label: Roll out the good crystal for his circle
choices.res: Word among the manors spreads fast—and {house}'s parlor fees climb right behind it.

choices.label: Keep a discreet private door for his guests (+prestige & renown)

overrides.desc: Discreet noble hospitality boosts {house} rich fees +35% and reputation +20%.

choices.res: Quiet side-door arrivals bring dukes who tip double simply to know nobody saw their crest.

pipe_trouble.title: Boiler Trouble at {house}
text: A copper main beneath {house} splits clean down the seam right after dawn, filling the laundry cellar with steam and leaving the upstairs tubs lukewarm until plumbers can patch the brass valves.

choices.label: Patch it weekly and endure the plumber's bill
choices.res: Rags, buckets, and cursing engineers trail through {house}'s cellar while repairs limp along.

choices.label: Pay overtime for immediate full copper replacement (-160g, fix it now)
choices.broke: Too steep this week—you'll have to let the slow patch crews work through it.
choices.res: Three dwarven smiths tear out the cracked joint before supper and restore scalding hot water across {house}.

street_musicians.title: Buskers Outside {house}
text: A trio of lute-players and a silver-voiced street singer set up beneath the corner lamp directly outside {house}. Passersby slow down to listen, tap their boots, and notice how warm {house}'s open windows look.

choices.label: Toss them a copper bowl and let them play
choices.res: Warm strings carry straight through {house}'s lounge and lure curious strollers inside.

choices.label: Put them on the house tab (-70g, +mood & stronger crowd)
choices.broke: They still play cheerfully for street coin without needing a house retainer.

overrides.desc: Paid musicians outside {house} lift demand +25% and propositions +20%.

choices.res: Hot cider and silver keep them playing your best hours right outside the awning.

wager_won.title: The Quarter Talks
text: Everyone from the spice stalls to the Velvet Thorn's own carriage step is repeating how {house} beat Isolde Thorne on the festival platform—and patrons are crowding your doorway to see the winner.

wager_lost.title: The Thorn Crows
text: Isolde wastes zero time letting every wine merchant and coachman know the Velvet Thorn carried the festival wager—pulling a few fair-weather regulars across the street for a couple of weeks.

title_patron.title: A Patron's Favor
text: A letter sealed in wax arrives for {name}. An old noble house she has charmed for months offers her a courtesy title: Lady {name}, with the household's name to back it.
An aging marchioness who never misses an evening at {house} has decided {name} deserves better than "Miss". The letters patent are already drawn up. All {name} has to do is accept.

accept.label: Accept graciously
accept.res: {name} accepts with a curtsy she has clearly practiced. The household sends flowers. The regulars start bowing, half as a joke, half not.

decline.label: Ask for something practical instead
decline.res: {name} thanks the house warmly and asks whether the honor might come as a donation. It does: {gold}.

image.comp: standing gracefully holding a wax-sealed parchment scroll, composed proud smile
image.setting: velvet parlor in a pleasure house, candelabra

title_fair.title: Crowning of the Street Fair
text: The Hollowmere street fair crowns a queen every year, chosen by the crowd. Half the market thinks {name} should enter. The entry fee is {gold}.
Bunting goes up across the square for the fair's crowning. Someone has already scrawled {name}'s name on the voting board. Entering officially costs {gold}.

enter.label: Enter her ({gold})
enter.win: The crowd roars. {name} walks the length of the square under a crown of paper lanterns, waving like she was born to it.
enter.lose: {name} comes a close second, and spends the evening being bought drinks by everyone who voted for her anyway.

skip.label: Not this year
skip.res: {name} watches the crowning from the edge of the square and cheers for the winner.

image.comp: standing beside a colorful street-fair voting board beneath bunting, amused confident smile
image.setting: sunny bustling town square street fair, colorful banners

title_arena.title: Challenge at the Guild Arena
text: The Adventurers' Guild is holding an exhibition bout and an open challenge. Word is the prize is {gold}, and the winner gets to call herself Champion. {name} is already stretching.
An open tournament at the Guild arena: anyone can enter, the winner takes {gold} and the title of Champion. {name} wants in.

fight.label: Let her fight
fight.win: Three bouts, three wins. {name} limps home with the purse, a split lip, and a grin that will not go away.

nightIncidents._readme: Report lines for the small night incidents (balance.json → incidents). bad = nobody handled it, ok = security (or Sam on watch) did. {house}, {guard} (who handled it), {lady} (the lady it happened to), {gold}.

brawl.label: Brawl

A fistfight broke out in the lounge at {house} and took a table and a lamp with it ({gold}).
ok: {guard} broke up a fight in the lounge before the first chair moved.
{guard} walked two red-faced brawlers out the door, one in each hand.
